sections.title: A verb that takes yourself as its object
sections.content: érez ("to feel") is normally used with a reflexive pronoun — magam ("myself"), magad ("yourself"), magát ("him/herself") — to say how someone feels. Rosszul érzem magam is literally "I feel myself badly", but it simply means "I feel bad/unwell". jól ('well') and rosszul ('badly') are the two adverbs you'll use here most.
magam/magad/magát is definite, so érez is conjugated with the definite ending here — érzem, not érzek. It's the same logic you already use with definite objects like a levest eszem.
